scope: Proposition 5.2 (Continuum complement gap) of the manuscript “Continuum Coulomb hardness with binary nuclear charges” (preprints/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 275 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 290f40f845dc3e0d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a constant g > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large D, (I − P)A(I − P) ≥ g(I − P). The inequality holds on the full one-particle form domain, including functions supported between the nuclei or at infinity.
